members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with Cartridge.
members.extended:
A Cartridge (Eyuboglu et al., 2025, [arXiv:2506.06266](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06266) — Cartridges: Lightweight and general-purpose long
context representations via self-study) is a trained key-value cache.  `num_virtual_tokens` learned
key/value pairs per attention layer are put in front of the model's cache, in place of a long document the
model would otherwise read at every query.  The first `num_frozen_tokens` of them stay fixed; the paper
recommends freezing one as an attention sink.  The cache is laid out as in prefix tuning, and starting it from
text or from a past cache is a separate step.

parameters.name: num_frozen_tokens
parameters.description: Initial virtual tokens that receive no gradient; not more than `num_virtual_tokens`.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import CartridgeConfig
>>> config = CartridgeConfig(num_virtual_tokens=16, num_frozen_tokens=2, task_type='CAUSAL_LM')
>>> config.num_virtual_tokens, config.num_frozen_tokens, config.peft_type
(16, 2, <PeftType.CARTRIDGE: 'CARTRIDGE'>)
>>> CartridgeConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True
notes:
Every field of the reference library's config is here, in its order and with its defaults, and
the config is read and written as `adapter_config.json`.  A field of the wrong type raises
`TypeError`.  `ValueError` is raised when `num_frozen_tokens` is negative or exceeds
`num_virtual_tokens`.  The cache starts as a random draw; `initialize_kv_prefix_from_text` and
`initialize_kv_prefix_from_past_key_values` (`lucid.peft`) replace it with the keys and values
of a document the model has read.

The cache is as wide as the model's attention: `token_dim` left out is `num_attention_heads`
times the head width the model's config declares (`head_dim`, `num_key_value_heads`), which is
the hidden size for most models and not for one whose heads are wider (T5-3B).  Where the model
declares them, a `token_dim` or `num_attention_heads` that disagrees raises `ValueError`.

members.name: CartridgeEncoder

methods.name: stored
methods.summary: The encoder's own tensors by the file's key: the trained rows are the file's `prompt_embeddings` (the frozen rows join them on the way out).

methods.name: __init__
methods.summary: Build the frozen and the trained rows of a cache `config` sizes, and draw them.

methods.name: from_config
methods.summary: The encoder for `config`; `word_embeddings` is not read.

methods.name: stores_prompt
methods.summary: `True`: the parameters are the cache itself, nothing maps them.

methods.name: num_embeddings
methods.summary: How many virtual tokens the cache holds: the frozen rows and the trained ones.

methods.name: indices
methods.summary: The virtual-token ids `(1, num_embeddings)` the encoder is called with.

methods.name: weight
methods.summary: The whole cache `(num_virtual_tokens, hidden)`: the frozen rows, then the trained ones.

methods.name: reset_parameters
methods.summary: Draw every row again from a standard normal.

methods.name: requires_grad_
methods.summary: Train (or freeze) the trained rows; the frozen rows are never trained.
methods.extended:
The tuner switches whole encoders on and off with this call, and a plain
`Module.requires_grad_` would make the frozen tokens trainable with the rest.

methods.name: load_prompt_embeddings
methods.summary: Copy a whole cache `(num_virtual_tokens, hidden)` in, the first rows into the frozen ones.

parameters.name: prompt_embeddings
parameters.description: The flattened cache an adapter file holds.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: The cache for each row of a batch: `(batch, ...)` ids to `(batch, num_virtual_tokens, hidden)`.
methods.extended: The ids are ignored; they are there so a cache is called as every prompt is.

methods.name: per_task
methods.summary: Whether the prompt depends on the task each batch row belongs to (`task_ids`).

methods.name: prompts
methods.summary: The prompt of each of `batch` rows: `(batch, num_embeddings, width)`.
methods.extended:
`tasks` is the task of each row, which a `per_task` encoder needs and the others
do not read.

methods.name: prompt_embeddings
methods.summary: The prompt as an adapter file stores it: `(rows, width)`, one row per virtual token.
methods.extended: A per-task encoder's is the shared prompt its tasks scale, which is what the file holds.

members.summary: A cache of keys and values that is trained, as a matrix of rows (one per virtual token) of every layer's key and value.
members.extended:
A row holds `2 * num_layers * token_dim` numbers laid out as prefix tuning's are, the key and the
value of each layer one after another, so the cache goes in front of the model's own like a
prefix's.  The first `num_frozen_tokens` rows are stored as a parameter that is never trained
(the Cartridges paper recommends freezing the first token as an attention sink), the rest as the
trained one.  Both start as a standard normal draw, which the reference's embedding table also
starts as; `load_prompt_embeddings` replaces them, from the first keys and values of a document
the model has read (`initialize_kv_prefix_from_text`), say.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
`num_virtual_tokens`, `num_layers`, `token_dim` (all set; the tuner fills them in from the
model), `num_frozen_tokens` and `inference_mode`.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.peft import CartridgeConfig, CartridgeEncoder
>>> config = CartridgeConfig(num_virtual_tokens=5, num_frozen_tokens=2, num_layers=3, token_dim=4)
>>> encoder = CartridgeEncoder(config)
>>> tuple(encoder.frozen_embedding.shape), tuple(encoder.trainable_embedding.shape)
((2, 24), (3, 24))
>>> encoder(lucid.zeros(2, 5).long()).shape
(2, 5, 24)
>>> encoder.frozen_embedding.requires_grad, encoder.trainable_embedding.requires_grad
(False, True)

attributes.name: frozen_embedding
attributes.description: `(num_frozen_tokens, hidden)` and never trained; `None` when no token is frozen.

methods.extended: The model runs as the base does, and its `modules_to_save` modules run their originals.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Call the model.
methods.extended: The prompt is put in by hooks on the model's own call, so nothing is applied here.

methods.name: get_model_config
methods.summary: `model`'s config as a dict, whatever it is held as.
methods.extended:
A config with a `to_dict` method is converted by it, a dataclass by `asdict`, a
mapping is copied.  A model with no `config` (or one that is `None`) has the
reference's stand-in, `{"model_type": "custom"}`, which is what the default target
modules and the prompt geometry read for a model of no known type.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to read the config of.

returns.description: The config's entries; a new dict, whose changes do not reach the model.

raises.description: `model.config` is none of a mapping, a dataclass or an object with `to_dict`.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraModel
>>> LoraModel.get_model_config(nn.Linear(2, 2))
{'model_type': 'custom'}

members.summary: The tuner of Cartridge: a `CartridgeEncoder` per adapter, read as every layer's cached keys and values.
members.extended:
The adapter file holds the cache whole as `prompt_embeddings`, frozen rows first; in memory the
frozen and the trained rows are two parameters, so loading splits the file's tensor and saving
joins them.

members.name: compose_cartridge_adapters
members.signature: compose_cartridge_adapters(adapter_paths: Sequence[str | os.PathLike[str]], output_path: str | os.PathLike[str], safe_serialization: bool = True)
members.summary: Join saved Cartridges into one by laying their caches end to end.
members.extended:
The composed cache is every cache one after another, so a model that reads it attends to all the
documents at once (the paper's composition by concatenation, done at the adapter, with no
several adapters at run time).  Its config is the first Cartridge's with `num_virtual_tokens`
the total; the frozen tokens are the first Cartridge's only, one attention sink for the whole.

parameters.name: adapter_paths
parameters.description: Directories of at least two saved Cartridges.

parameters.name: output_path
parameters.description: The directory to write the composed adapter to; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Write `adapter_model.safetensors`, the one format here; `False` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

raises.description:
Fewer than two paths, an adapter that is not a Cartridge, Cartridges whose sizes differ, or a
directory without a `prompt_embeddings` tensor.

members.summary: Start a Cartridge (or an unprojected prefix) from the keys and values of a cache you have.
members.extended:
The first `num_virtual_tokens` tokens of the cache of one sequence become the adapter's rows
(`prompt_embeddings_from_past_key_values`), frozen ones first.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: A model with a `CARTRIDGE` or `PREFIX_TUNING` adapter.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: The adapter to initialise; the active one when left out.

parameters.name: past_key_values
parameters.description: The cache, in a form `prompt_embeddings_from_past_key_values` takes.

parameters.name: num_virtual_tokens
parameters.description: How many leading tokens to take; the adapter's own count when left out.

raises.description:
The adapter is neither a Cartridge nor a prefix, is a prefix with `prefix_projection`, or the
cache does not fit (see `prompt_embeddings_from_past_key_values`); the adapter's rows are
untouched then.

members.name: initialize_kv_prefix_from_text
members.signature: initialize_kv_prefix_from_text(model: PeftModel, tokenizer: _TextEncoder, text: str, adapter_name: str | None = None, num_virtual_tokens: int | None = None, use_chat_template: bool = True, max_length: int | None = None)
members.summary: Start a Cartridge from a text: read it with the model, and keep the first keys and values.
members.extended:
The base model runs over the text with the adapters off (`use_cache=True`), and the first
`num_virtual_tokens` entries of the cache it returns are loaded into the adapter
(`initialize_kv_prefix_from_past_key_values`).  No tokenizer package is needed: `tokenizer`
is any object with `encode(text) -> list[int]`, as the ones of `lucid.utils.tokenizer` are,
and one that also has `apply_chat_template` reads the text as a system message.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description:
A model with a `CARTRIDGE` or `PREFIX_TUNING` adapter, whose base model returns its
cache as `past_key_values` when called with `use_cache=True`.

parameters.name: tokenizer
parameters.description: Turns the text into token ids.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The document, or the first part of it.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: The adapter to initialise; the active one when left out.

parameters.name: num_virtual_tokens
parameters.description: How many leading tokens to keep; the adapter's own count when left out.

parameters.name: use_chat_template
parameters.description: Read the text through the tokenizer's chat template as a system message when it has one.

parameters.name: max_length
parameters.description: Cut the token ids to this many before the model reads them.

raises.description:
`tokenizer` offers neither `encode` nor a chat template, or returns something that is
not token ids.

The adapter cannot be initialised from a cache (see
`initialize_kv_prefix_from_past_key_values`), the text has no tokens, or the model returned
no cache.

members.name: prompt_embeddings_from_past_key_values
members.summary: Pack the first keys and values of a cache into the matrix an adapter file holds.
members.extended:
Row $t$ is the key and the value of token $t$ for layer 0, then for layer 1, and so
on, each of the `heads * head_dim` numbers a layer keeps per token; that is the layout prefix
tuning's and a Cartridge's `prompt_embeddings` have, so the matrix can be loaded into either.

parameters.name: past_key_values
parameters.description:
The cache of one sequence: a legacy tuple (or list) of `(key, value)` per layer, an object
with `to_legacy_cache()` (`lucid.utils.cache.DynamicCache`), or an iterable of
`(key, value)` tuples.  Each tensor is `(1, heads, tokens, head_dim)`.

parameters.name: num_virtual_tokens
parameters.description: How many leading tokens to keep.

returns.description: `(num_virtual_tokens, num_layers * 2 * heads * head_dim)`, in the cache's dtype and device.

raises.description: `past_key_values` is none of the three accepted kinds, or a layer of it is not a pair of tensors.

The cache is empty, is of a batch (not one sequence), holds fewer than `num_virtual_tokens`
tokens, or its layers disagree on heads, head size or length.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.peft import prompt_embeddings_from_past_key_values
>>> layer = (lucid.zeros(1, 2, 5, 4), lucid.ones(1, 2, 5, 4))
>>> prompt_embeddings_from_past_key_values((layer, layer), num_virtual_tokens=3).shape
(3, 32)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.cartridge` — Cartridge: a trained key-value cache that stands in for a long document.
extended:
Cartridge (Eyuboglu et al., 2025, [arXiv:2506.06266](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06266)) is a trained key-value cache: `num_virtual_tokens`
learned key and value pairs per attention layer, put in front of the model's own in place of a long
document it would otherwise read at every query.  It is trained by self-study, with the model
answering questions about the document, and a Cartridge for a corpus costs a fraction of the memory
of the corpus in context.  Pick it for serving many queries over one large, unchanging document.

The cache is laid out and applied as prefix tuning's is, but it is stored directly, not produced by
a projection, so a Cartridge can be started from the keys and values the model makes of a text
(`initialize_kv_prefix_from_text`) and several can be joined (`compose_cartridge_adapters`).  The
first `num_frozen_tokens` rows are never trained: the paper keeps one as an attention sink.

Here: `CartridgeEncoder` (the cache, trained) and `CartridgeModel` (the tuner), the config, and
the four utilities of `lucid.peft.tuners.cartridge.utils`.  `CartridgeConfig`, `CartridgeEncoder`
and the utilities are exported from `lucid.peft`, as the reference exports them; the tuner is not,
the reference having no model class.  Importing the package registers the method (its config under
`PeftType.CARTRIDGE`, its tuner and encoder), which is what makes `get_peft_model` and
`PeftModel.from_pretrained` know it.
citation: Eyuboglu, Sabri, et al. "Cartridges: Lightweight and General-Purpose Long Context Representations via Self-Study." [arXiv:2506.06266](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06266), 2025.
theory:
A Cartridge (Eyuboglu et al., 2025, [arXiv:2506.06266](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06266) — Cartridges: Lightweight and general-purpose long
context representations via self-study) is a trained key-value cache.  `num_virtual_tokens` learned
key/value pairs per attention layer are put in front of the model's cache, in place of a long document the
model would otherwise read at every query.  The first `num_frozen_tokens` of them stay fixed; the paper
recommends freezing one as an attention sink.  The cache is laid out as in prefix tuning, and starting it from
text or from a past cache is a separate step.
